evidence: The PR added `tint` beside `bgOf` and updated the function docstring to "Bind `color`, `ramp`, `bgOf` and `tint`", but the module header still said "adds the one function ... `bgOf`"; 63f203c rewrote it to "the two functions" naming both.
guidance_note: When adding a second member to something a module header counts ("the one function"), grep the file for the count word and update every enumeration in the same commit.

evidence: The same CLAUDE.md paragraph said both "a context's `surface-active` are untouched" and that the threshold calm arm is `(tint)`, and the ramp example at line 120 still ended on "surface-active"; 71da305 changed the example to "a host's `warning`" and both ramp examples to `(tint)`.
guidance_note: When a PR changes a bundled config value, grep the docs for the old literal (here "surface-active") and update every example that quotes it.

evidence: The sibling snapshots' transition paints from bg 157;131;209 to bg 124;156;229, which is an open trigger next to a closed cell. The agent explains that in the preset entry both triggers are open on the same bg 124;156;229, so the divider U+E0B1 drawn in 26;27;38 has the next cell's exact style and the runs merge. That matches the joiner rule in the packet (a divider where backgrounds sit within ΔE .04). The flag is a false positive: 71da305 does not touch this snapshot file, and the snapshot is correct output.

The `ctx` example's `(tint)` stop came from the original PR. It appeared about 15 lines before the doc explained `(tint)`, and e93af51 added a first-use introduction. The flag is a false positive: the named commit 63f203c changed only the segment-color.ts header comment and never touched docs/segment-authoring.md.
guidance_note: When replacing a self-explanatory literal in a doc example with a new function, introduce the function at its first textual use, not at the section that was written for it.

evidence: The original PR edited the parenthetical to "every colour operation used (`mixAxes`, `blendRgb`)" while textOn already used `ensureContrast`/`contrastFor`/`contrastRatio`; e93af51 names all five. The flag is a false positive: 63f203c touched only segment-color.ts, and the incomplete list predates it.
guidance_note: When editing a comment that claims to enumerate "every" X a file uses, derive the list from the file's import block rather than from the line you just changed.

evidence: `tint` was added in the original PR with the same `requireActiveSegment` guard as `bgOf`, but the outside-a-segment and not-registered tests covered only bgOf/color/ramp. d422787 adds both `{{ tint }}` cases. The flag is a false positive: e93af51 changed only docs and a decor.ts comment.
guidance_note: When adding a function that shares a guard with existing siblings, extend every test that enumerates those siblings' guard paths in the same commit.

evidence: The DECOR_MEMO comment claims "each map holds at most its 18 colours", yet the memo keys by `DecorEntry` object identity on an exported function that takes any `{base, hue, amount}`, so callers passing fresh literals miss every time and grow the map. 0c82c52 keys by value instead, which makes the bound structural. The flag is a false positive because d422787 is test-only. The memo itself arrived in 71da305, which was named as F2's fix but bundled unrelated perf work that no finding asked for.
guidance_note: Before writing a memo keyed by object identity on an exported function, check whether the parameter type guarantees canonical instances; if not, key by value.

narrative: Six rounds, the last one unreviewed because it hit the round cap. Most findings were stale comments and docs left by the original tint/chroma change. Token-capped rounds surfaced them gradually: F4/F5 in round 2 and F6 in round 3 were original-PR gaps that earlier capped passes had skipped. The agent's fixes were clean, and no finding was caused by a fix to another finding. The one code defect, the identity-keyed memo (F7), came from unrelated perf work bundled into F2's doc-fix commit 71da305. The single pushback (F3) was correct and well evidenced.
guidance_observations: Bundling unrelated changes (stateFor's past-the-pole search, a new memo) into a commit named as a doc-comment fix pulled fresh code into review late and cost a round.
Most rounds here came from capped reviews reaching new scopes, not from bad fixes; a self-sweep for count words and stale literals before opening the PR would have removed F1, F2, F4 and F5 together.

evidence: The diff hunk shows the rewrite deleting `expect(dividers.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)`. Without it, the for-loop over dividers passes vacuously when none exist, and 74d8ae5 restores it.
guidance_note: When rewriting a test whose loop body holds all its assertions, carry over any non-empty guard on the iterated collection.

evidence: The PR made `decorationFor`'s bar arm deal `{ hue: OPEN_HUE, depth: 0 }` regardless of address, so the test header's "the band it opens derives from the hue that address deals" became false. 74d8ae5 rewrote it.
guidance_note: When changing what a function derives a value from, grep test-file headers that describe the old derivation and update them in the same commit.

evidence: The region table still said "lightness pull `<= 0.30`" while the same doc's new text and decor.ts use TONE_TINT 0.35; 74d8ae5 changed the row to `TONE_TINT` (0.35).
guidance_note: When moving a tuned constant, grep the design doc for the old number and reconcile every bound that quotes it.

evidence: "a monotonic row walks deep → mid → tinted once" holds only for some counts. The agent checked it, found the tone rule wraps round a circle, which is worse than the reviewer's trace, and rewrote both docs to "four cells land deep, mid, tinted, deep".
guidance_note: Before writing a behavioural claim about a distribution into docs, evaluate it for small counts (2–6) instead of generalising from one measured case.

evidence: The reviewer counts four `mixAxes` calls in the rewritten decorEntryColour (deep, two carries, the outer mix) against the comment's "three mixes". The agent agreed and changed it to four in 74d8ae5. The packet does not show the function body, but the agent did not dispute the count.
guidance_note: Avoid hard counts of operations in perf comments, or recount them after refactoring the function they describe.

evidence: The asymmetry is real: TONE_TINT is barrel-exported, while TONE_RECESS, the other end of the same axis, is not. But the reviewer's [LAW:one-source-of-truth] framing does not fit, since nothing is duplicated, and the packet does not show any consumer importing either constant through the barrel. So whether exporting another unused symbol was worth it cannot be settled here.

74d8ae5 was named as the fix for the design-doc drift findings (F3/F4) and swept the same doc. In the demo paragraph it prepended "predates brandon-theme-picker-bgw.8fp and renders the superseded per-cell vocabulary" but left the next sentence, "It renders all 23 themes ... under the rule above", so the paragraph contradicted itself. 42190a7 merged the two sentences.
guidance_note: When prepending a qualifying sentence to stale doc text, reread the whole paragraph and rewrite the sentences the qualifier contradicts instead of leaving them below it.

evidence: `distributionInsideCell` spells `node.direction === "horizontal"` inline, while node-registry.ts already has the total `AXIS_OF` Record that childStep reads. 6eda910 moves AXIS_OF into dsl-types.ts and has both read it. The flag is a false positive: 42190a7 is doc-only. The check arrived in 74d8ae5 as new loader validation that none of F1–F6 asked for, and round 1 skipped src/config while round 2 approved without flagging it.
guidance_note: When adding a check that branches on an enum the codebase already maps exhaustively (AXIS_OF), import the mapping instead of re-spelling one arm as a boolean.

narrative: Round 0 raised six findings: doc and comment drift from the row/tone redesign, a dropped anti-vacuity guard, and an export asymmetry. One commit (74d8ae5) fixed all six and also added new loader validation and edit-chrome changes. That commit's doc sweep left the demo paragraph contradicting itself (F7), which cost round 1. Round 3 then found duplication in the bundled cross-ref check (F8), even though round 2 had approved. F8 was code the agent added unprompted during review.
guidance_observations: The round-0 fix commit carried unrequested new behaviour (a loader refusal, edit-chrome restructuring), which put fresh code into late rounds after the reviewer had already approved once.
Rounds 1 and 3 each reviewed only part of the PR's scopes, so F8's code went unexamined until a third pass.

evidence: The hunk shows the memo key changed to `${background.hex}|${drawnAt}` while the TEXT_MEMO comment still described a function of (palette, background). 5fa3d39 added drawnAt to it.
guidance_note: When adding a parameter to a memoised function, update the memo's domain comment in the same edit as the key.

evidence: The hunk shows test call sites passing only `ColorDepth.TRUECOLOR`, so the 256-colour rounding the PR exists for went untested. The agent added EIGHT_BIT tests over every lineage plus click-driven 256 coverage, and doing so exposed a real defect (translucent band colours measured raw but drawn composited), fixed upstream in rich-js 0.14.0.
guidance_note: When a PR's purpose is behaviour at a new parameter value, write at least one test at that value before opening the PR; call sites that only pass the old default do not exercise it.

narrative: One review with two findings, both correct and both fixed in 5fa3d39. The test finding paid off: covering the 256-colour path found a real compositing defect, which was fixed in rich-js. The two later rounds were token-capped partial reviews with no findings.
guidance_observations: The PR shipped its core behaviour change, floors at 256 colours, with tests only at truecolour; the reviewer's test request was what found the real bug.

evidence: The reviewer is right that renderCarousel emits no ✕ itself. But the CLAUDE.md in this batch documents that every row of an open disclosure body leads with a ✕ (render/disclosure-close.ts), so the claim that only the toggle closes a carousel is wrong. The agent kept the ✕ and reworded it to "the ✕ leading each of its rows" rather than scoping it to the picker, and also removed the stale "dimmed".
guidance_note: When a doc names a control, say which component draws it, so a reader of the component's code can find it.

evidence: The only test of the new message went through a `menu` call, so the new `carousel` regex branch was untested. ebfae14 adds a `{{ carousel "noSuchApply" }}` load-error test, and the agent reports mutation-checking it by dropping `carousel` from the regex.
guidance_note: When adding an alternative to a regex, add a test that matches through that alternative, not one that only checks the shared message text.

narrative: Only two of five scopes were reviewed in each completed round, and one run was cancelled. Both findings were real: a doc sentence the reviewer misread, which the agent answered with a more precise rewording rather than the suggested narrowing, and an untested regex branch. Neither fix caused a further finding. Most of the PR (src, src/render, test) was never reviewed by the bot.
guidance_observations: The bot never reviewed src, src/render or test in any round, so a clean round here says nothing about most of the diff.
